You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From cb0b430b4e3acc88c85e0ad2e25f2a25a5765262 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Miaoqian Lin <linmq006@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Mar 2022 08:26:02 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] net: dsa: Add missing of_node_put() in dsa_port_parse_of

The device_node pointer is returned by of_parse_phandle()  with refcount
incremented. We should use of_node_put() on it when done.

Fixes: 6d4e5c570c2d ("net: dsa: get port type at parse time")
Signed-off-by: Miaoqian Lin <linmq006@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220316082602.10785-1-linmq006@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/net/dsa/dsa2.c b/net/dsa/dsa2.c
index 074e4a69a728..88e2808019b4 100644
--- a/net/dsa/dsa2.c
+++ b/net/dsa/dsa2.c
@@ -1436,6 +1436,7 @@ static int dsa_port_parse_of(struct dsa_port *dp, struct device_node *dn)
 		const char *user_protocol;
 
 		master = of_find_net_device_by_node(ethernet);
+		of_node_put(ethernet);
 		if (!master)
 			return -EPROBE_DEFER;
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/dsa/dsa2.c`**
   - A new line was added to call `of_node_put(ethernet);` after the `master` variable is assigned the result of `of_find_net_device_by_node(ethernet);`. This ensures that the reference count of the `ethernet` device node is decremented properly, preventing a potential memory leak.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a memory management issue related to the reference counting of device nodes in the Device Tree. The added `of_node_put()` call is necessary because `of_find_net_device_by_node()` increments the reference count of the `ethernet` device node. By adding this line, the patch ensures that the reference count is decremented appropriately when the device node is no longer needed, thus fixing the bug introduced in a previous commit (identified by the Fixes tag).

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
struct device_node *ethernet = of_parse_phandle(dn, "ethernet", 0);
master = of_find_net_device_by_node(ethernet);
```
Reason:
The `of_parse_phandle()` function increments the reference count of the `ethernet` device node when it retrieves it. However, there is no corresponding call to `of_node_put()` to decrement the reference count after the node is no longer needed, leading to a memory leak.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
of_node_put(ethernet);
```
Reason:
The addition of `of_node_put(ethernet);` ensures that the reference count of the `ethernet` device node is decremented after it has been used. This prevents the memory leak by properly releasing the reference when the device node is no longer needed.
